t: Formed from Upper Peru in 1825 and named after Simón Bolívar, with Sucre as constitutional capital and La Paz as seat of government.
Lost wars cost it the Pacific coast to Chile, Acre to Brazil and most of the Chaco to Paraguay.
Its 1952 revolution and the election of Evo Morales made it a landmark of Latin American social and indigenous politics.
dyk: Landlocked since the War of the Pacific, Bolivia still maintains a navy, which patrols Lake Titicaca and the country’s rivers.
ev: Upper Peru declares independence at Chuquisaca as the Republic of Bolívar
Andrés de Santa Cruz forms the Peru-Bolivian Confederation
Chile occupies Antofagasta, beginning the War of the Pacific
The Treaty of Petrópolis cedes Acre to Brazil
The Chaco War with Paraguay begins
The National Revolution brings universal suffrage and nationalises the mines
Evo Morales becomes Bolivia’s first indigenous president
A new constitution creates the Plurinational State of Bolivia

f.capital: Sucre (constitutional); La Paz (seat of government from 1899)
f.founder: Antonio José de Sucre; Simón Bolívar
